# Federal Register Summary — PFAS Drinking Water Standards

The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has finalized National Primary
Drinking Water Regulations for per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances, commonly
known as PFAS. The rule sets enforceable maximum contaminant levels for six
specific PFAS compounds.

## Regulated compounds

The final rule sets a Maximum Contaminant Level (MCL) of 4 parts per
trillion for each of PFOA and PFOS. PFHxS, PFNA, and HFPO-DA each receive
an MCL of 10 parts per trillion. Mixtures of PFHxS, PFNA, HFPO-DA, and
PFBS are regulated collectively under a Hazard Index approach.

## Compliance timeline

Public water systems have three years from the effective date to complete
initial monitoring. Systems that identify PFAS above the MCL must implement
treatment or take other action to reduce PFAS within five years of the
effective date.

## Health context

EPA's health effects assessment notes that chronic exposure to PFOA and
PFOS has been associated with decreased antibody response to vaccines,
dyslipidemia, decreased infant and fetal growth, and increased risk of
certain cancers.
